name: Tung Chee Chen
current_role: Former chairman & CEO of Orient Overseas (International) Ltd (OOCL parent); private investor; Monaco's honorary consul in Hong Kong
profile: Second son of shipping magnate C.Y. Tung and younger brother of Hong Kong's first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa. Ran Orient Overseas (OOCL) as chairman/CEO from 1996; in 2018 he and his brother sold the family's 68.7% stake to COSCO for about $4.3bn. Now largely retired from executive roles.
interesting_fact: He trained as an engineer: a bachelor's degree from the University of Liverpool and a master's in mechanical engineering from MIT, before joining the family shipping group.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired the Institute for Shipboard Education Foundation, which oversees Semester at Sea, the floating-university program his father C.Y. Tung was instrumental in founding.
notes: No personal public channels found. His brother Tung Chee-hwa died in Sept 2026 (per Baird Maritime), so avoid outreach timing insensitivity. Any route would likely be via OOCL/Tung family office; Semester at Sea link is a soft angle.

name: Won-Woo Kim
current_role: President (사장) and head of Digital Strategy, NICE Holdings (largest shareholder of NICE Group), promoted in the 2026 executive reshuffle
profile: Kim Won-woo (김원우, b. ~1993) is the eldest son of NICE Group founder Kim Kwang-soo, who died in 2018 at 55; he inherited control at age 25 and is the largest shareholder of NICE Holdings, parent of Korea's leading credit bureau NICE Information Service. He has worked in the group's digital strategy unit, becoming executive director in Dec 2024 and president for 2026.
interesting_fact: He became controlling owner of one of Korea's biggest credit-information groups at just 25; day-to-day management has been run by professional CEO Choi Young while he built experience in digital strategy.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Korean-language press only. Best route is via NICE Holdings corporate communications.

name: Mark Leonard
current_role: Founder of Constellation Software; former president (stepped down Sept 2025 for health reasons), left the board May 2026, now adviser on its Permanent Engaged Minority Shareholder (PEMS) strategy
profile: After an MBA from Western Ontario and ~11 years in venture capital, Leonard founded Toronto's Constellation Software in 1995; it has bought 850+ vertical-market software businesses and holds them permanently. He and family own ~7%. He resigned as president in Sept 2025 and did not stand for re-election to the board in May 2026, staying on as an adviser.
interesting_fact: Famously elusive: he has almost never spoken to the press, and before CSI he worked as a banker, valuator, mason, gravedigger, dog handler, bouncer, sapper and wind energy researcher (Globe and Mail via Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: Despite building a multibillion-dollar company, his reported compensation as president was a symbolic C$1 base salary with no bonus or stock awards.
notes: Extremely private; famously never gives interviews; stepped back for health reasons in 2025, so an interview request is unlikely to succeed. His annual President's letters (csisoftware.com) are the best way to show familiarity. Route via Constellation corporate.

name: Xue Min
current_role: Founder and chairman of United Imaging Group (联影集团), controlling shareholder of Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare (688271.SS)
profile: Xue Min (薛敏, b. 1957) studied physics at Fudan and earned an MRI-physics master's in Wuhan before PhD studies in biomedical engineering at Case Western Reserve/Cleveland Clinic. He founded Shenzhen Mindit (MRI) in 1998, later sold to Siemens, then in 2011 founded United Imaging to challenge GE, Siemens and Philips; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022.
interesting_fact: United Imaging set out from day one to develop every product line and core technology in-house; within about a decade it had launched over 260 products, including China's own 1.5T MRI magnet.
deep_cut_fact: After 100-plus days of intensive work, United Imaging's very first image, produced in 2011-12, was a scan of Xue Min's own right foot.
notes: Chinese-language press mostly. Zhang Qiang is chairman/CEO of the listed United Imaging Healthcare; Xue chairs the parent group. IR email is the listed company's.

name: Mark Davis
current_role: Owner and managing general partner, Las Vegas Raiders (NFL); owner, Las Vegas Aces (WNBA)
profile: Son of Raiders legend Al Davis, Mark Davis spent his whole career inside the team, starting in the equipment room and team retail, and inherited control after his father's death in 2011. He moved the franchise from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 and Allegiant Stadium; the team is now valued at over $7bn (vs $761m in 2011). He bought the WNBA's Aces in 2021.
interesting_fact: While working in Raiders team retail he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer now used across the NFL.
deep_cut_fact: A Chico State alumnus, he long kept driving from Oakland back to Chico to see his favourite barber for his trademark bowl cut, and famously drove a 1997 Dodge Caravan with a VHS player.
notes: Approachable, unpretentious reputation but gives few long interviews (ESPN's Tim Keown profile is a rare one). Aces dynasty (WNBA titles) and Las Vegas stadium economics are natural podcast angles. Route via Raiders communications department.

name: Adam Kwok
current_role: Executive director, Sun Hung Kai Properties (since 2014); runs SHKP's South China property business
profile: Adam Kwok Kai-fai (郭基煇) is a grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and son of former joint chairman Thomas Kwok. After a stint in investment banking he joined Hong Kong's largest developer in 2008, became an executive director in 2014 and has led its South China (mainland) property business since 2013, acting as project director on major residential and commercial schemes.
interesting_fact: He is part of one of Asia's richest property families: four of his cousins, his father, an uncle and his grandmother have all been billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: A keen cyclist, he donated HK$10 million to a Hong Kong Sports Institute / HKUST joint venture to develop more aerodynamic cycling equipment for Hong Kong riders.
notes: Also sits on HK government's Major Sports Events Committee and is a vice president of REDA. Avoid referencing his father's conviction. Route via SHKP corporate communications.

name: Jin Sook Chang
current_role: Co-founder and former chief merchandising officer of Forever 21 (no longer involved since the 2019-20 bankruptcy sale)
profile: Korean-born Jin Sook Chang emigrated to Los Angeles in 1981 with husband Do Won Chang; in 1984 they opened a 900 sq ft store, Fashion 21, in Highland Park and built it into Forever 21, a fast-fashion chain with ~600 stores and 30,000 staff by 2015, where she ran merchandising. The company went bankrupt in 2019 and was sold in 2020; she is no longer listed as a billionaire.
interesting_fact: The couple are devout Christians, which is why 'John 3:16' was printed on the bottom of every Forever 21 shopping bag.
deep_cut_fact: The empire began as a 900-square-foot shop called 'Fashion 21' in LA's Highland Park, opened in 1984 with just $11,000 in savings.
notes: No longer a billionaire (Forbes, July 2019) and no public activity found since 2020; very private. Avoid the bankruptcy as a topic. Profile is shared with husband Do Won Chang. No published contact channels.

name: Nandlal Rungta
current_role: Long-serving director of Rungta Mines Ltd (on the board since January 1985); the group is now chaired by Siddharth Rungta
profile: Nandlal Rungta is the patriarch behind Rungta Mines, a privately held Kolkata/Chaibasa-based iron-ore, manganese and steel group incorporated in 1962 that has expanded into integrated steel plants (five facilities in Odisha, one in Jharkhand), TMT bars under the Rungta Steel brand, construction and power. Day-to-day leadership has passed to the next generation under chairman Siddharth Rungta.
interesting_fact: Rungta Mines is one of India's largest private merchant iron-ore miners yet remains an unlisted company, and has diversified from mining into integrated steelmaking and captive power.
notes: Extremely low public profile; virtually no interviews or press. Wealth lists (360 ONE) now credit 'Siddharth Rungta and family'. Alive status inferred from his still-active directorships (tofler.in), not a dated source. Corporate route only.

name: Wang Jian
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, BGI Group (parent of Shenzhen-listed BGI Genomics, 300676.SZ)
profile: Wang Jian (汪建, b. 1954) trained in medicine in China, did postdoctoral research at the Universities of Texas and Iowa and was a research fellow at the University of Washington (1990-94). He co-founded BGI in 1999 to take on China's share of the Human Genome Project and built it into one of the world's largest genomics groups (sequencing, BGI Genomics, MGI Tech). He also co-founded iCarbonX.
interesting_fact: BGI was founded in 1999 to deliver China's 1% contribution to the international Human Genome Project, and grew into one of the world's largest genome-sequencing organisations.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2024, aged 70, he led a BGI science team to the summit of Everest via the north side, his second ascent 14 years after first summiting with Vanke founder Wang Shi in 2010, setting a record as the oldest Chinese person to summit; the team collected ultrasound and EEG data at the top.
notes: Outspoken, media-friendly in Chinese press; known for extreme-sport stunts (Everest, etc.) used to promote health data science. ir@bgi.com is BGI Genomics' listed IR address, not personal.

name: Kalanithi Maran
current_role: Founder, executive chairman and managing director, Sun TV Network / Sun Group
profile: Son of former Union minister Murasoli Maran, he launched Sun TV in 1993 and built Sun Group into a south-Indian media giant: 37 channels reaching 140m+ households, newspapers, FM radio, DTH, Sun Pictures and a Hindi channel (Sun Neo, 2024). Sun also owns cricket franchises Sunrisers Hyderabad (IPL), Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20) and Sunrisers Leeds (The Hundred). He owned SpiceJet 2010-15.
interesting_fact: Sun Group's cricket empire spans three countries: Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL, Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20 champions) in South Africa and, since 2025, Sunrisers Leeds in England's The Hundred.
deep_cut_fact: After Don Bosco and Loyola College in Chennai, he went to the US for an MBA at the University of Scranton in Pennsylvania, where the abundance of TV channels (vs India's single state broadcaster) is said to have inspired Sun TV.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. tvinfo@sunnetwork.in is Sun TV's general company email from exchange filings (not a dedicated press address). Avoid the family share dispute and old telecom case.

name: Li Zhe
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Riverside Investment Group (Beijing) as of 2018; current status not confirmed
profile: Li Zhe (李喆) leads the Riverside Group, a Beijing-based developer focused on real estate, healthcare/senior living, tourism and entertainment, which developed the Beijing Jinhai Lake International Tourism Resort. In the late 2010s Riverside partnered with Six Flags to build Six Flags-branded theme parks across China; Hurun listed him through 2020.
interesting_fact: Under Li, Riverside signed on to bring Six Flags theme parks to China, including separate 'Six Flags Adventure World' and 'Six Flags Kids World' concepts; he was named to blooloop's 2018 Theme Park Influencer list.
deep_cut_fact: He has served on the World Best Practices Steering Committee of UN-Habitat and as a director with The Nature Conservancy, alongside the Chinese People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries.
notes: Identity match (Hurun 'Riverside' real estate, 2008-2020) is likely but not confirmed with a Chinese-language source. Six Flags ended its China partnership with Riverside in 2020 and he dropped off rich lists afterwards; current role and wealth are unclear. Treat as low priority.

name: Carolus Nolet, Sr.
current_role: Chairman, Nolet Distillery (Schiedam, Netherlands); 10th-generation head of the family that co-owns Ketel One with Diageo
profile: Carolus Nolet Sr. (b. 1941) joined his family's 1691-founded Schiedam distillery in 1962 and took it over in 1979. After touring US bars from 1983 he created Ketel One, a pot-distilled premium vodka, landing its first US case sale in 1989; in 2009 Diageo bought 50% of Ketel One for $900m. He later launched NOLET'S gin and remains chairman, with sons Carl Jr. and Bob running the business.
interesting_fact: Ketel One is named after Distilleerketel #1, the coal-fired copper pot still at the Nolet distillery, a method normally used for jenever and whisky rather than vodka.
deep_cut_fact: Ketel One's first-ever case sale came in 1989 from Doug Biederbeck of Bix restaurant in San Francisco; Nolet's own after-dinner drink is a Vesper made with 50% Ketel One and 50% NOLET'S Silver gin, stirred over ice.
notes: In his mid-80s; sons Carl Jr. and Bob Nolet are the active executives and more accessible for interviews. Last on Forbes list 2015-17. Alive status assumed from lack of any obituary; not explicitly confirmed with a dated 2026 source.

name: Chetan Dube
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO, Quant (Quant AI), New York agentic-AI 'digital employee' company (founded 2024)
profile: Indian-born Dube was an applied-mathematics professor at NYU before founding IPsoft in 1998, which became conversational-AI firm Amelia (renamed 2020) serving ~500 corporate clients. SoundHound acquired Amelia in Aug 2024 and Dube left to start Quant, which builds agentic 'digital employees' for contact centres and partners with IBM (e.g. 'Ava' at reinsurer Fortitude Re). He is no longer on billionaire lists.
interesting_fact: He spoke at IBM Think in May 2026 on the 'agentic enterprise', and Quant's agents are sold via IBM, including a bilingual English/Spanish AI contact centre for Fortitude Re.
deep_cut_fact: His AI platform Amelia (2014), and later the whole company in its 2020 rebrand, was named after aviator Amelia Earhart, whose habit of pushing against the limits of her era Dube said he wanted the technology to emulate.
notes: Very media-active: writes bylines (CSQ, Entrepreneur UK), speaks at conferences, and is a strong fit for an AI/data-center podcast. Avoid framing the Amelia sale price vs funding raised. Best route: Quant's website/press or LinkedIn.

name: Cheng Zhuo
current_role: Founder, chairwoman and executive director, Circuit Fabology Microelectronics Equipment (CFME, 芯碁微装; 688630.SS, Hong Kong dual listing 2026)
profile: Cheng Zhuo (程卓, b. May 1966) is the founder and controlling shareholder of Hefei-based CFME, a maker of maskless direct-write lithography equipment for PCBs and semiconductors/advanced packaging. She founded it in 2015 after handling the restructuring of lithography firm Hefei Xinshuo, listed it on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021 and passed a Hong Kong listing hearing in June 2026.
interesting_fact: She came to chip-equipment from finance and management, not engineering: she was drawn into the industry in 2013 when asked to help restructure Hefei Xinshuo's debts, briefly serving as its chair and finance director before founding CFME in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Her career began in August 1984 in management at state-owned Factory 9409 (Anhui General Machinery); after leaving in 1998 she founded businesses including Anhui Shengjia Auction Co. before moving into lithography. She studied mechanics at a technical school and Chinese literature at Anhui Radio & TV University.
notes: Low-profile; Chinese-language coverage only. Contact via CFME's board secretary / IR office (details in company filings on cninfo.com.cn). Lithography for AI-server PCBs/advanced packaging is a relevant data-center angle.

name: Sergei Studennikov
current_role: Founder of Krasnoye & Beloye (Red & White); co-owner (with wife, ~49%) of Mercury Retail Group (Krasnoye & Beloye, Bristol, Dixy)
profile: Born in 1967 in Stavropol Krai and raised in Chelyabinsk Oblast, Studennikov founded the SPS holding distributing vodka, beer and tobacco in the late 1980s/90s, then opened the first Krasnoye & Beloye store in Kopeysk in 2006. In 2019 he merged it with Bristol and Dixy (Kesaev/Katsiev) into Mercury Retail, Russia's largest alcohol retailer with ~15,000+ stores; its IPO was shelved in 2022.
interesting_fact: Krasnoye & Beloye grew from a single store in Kopeysk in 2006 to about 6,700 stores by 2018 and is now Russia's largest liquor retailer.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, he graduated from the Satka mining and ceramics technical school and worked in that trade; in 1998 he opened a large tile store, and he also helped launch the Evrograd DIY chain and the Monetka grocery chain.
notes: Very private; gave a rare major interview to RBC in Nov 2024. Russia-based alcohol retailer: consider sanctions/reputational context before outreach. No published personal or office contacts found.

name: Qiu Jianlin
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Hengyi Group; chairman of Hengyi Industries (Brunei refinery JV)
profile: Qiu Jianlin (邱建林) built Hangzhou-based Zhejiang Hengyi Group into one of China's largest polyester, PTA and caprolactam producers, controlling Shenzhen-listed Hengyi Petrochemical (000703, now chaired by Qiu Yibo). Hengyi integrated upstream into oil refining via the Pulau Muara Besar refinery in Brunei, a 70/30 JV with the Brunei government that started up in 2019.
interesting_fact: Hengyi's Brunei refinery and petrochemical complex at Pulau Muara Besar is Brunei's largest integrated refinery and one of the biggest Chinese investments in the country, with a ~$12bn second phase planned.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2013 Oxford Business Group interview he explained the Brunei bet: 'Politically and economically Brunei Darussalam has shown itself to be one of the best locations for foreign investment.'
notes: Low public profile in English media. Day-to-day leadership of listed Hengyi Petrochemical has passed to the next generation (Qiu Yibo, who gives interviews). Energy/refining angle fits the podcast. Corporate contact via Hengyi Petrochemical board office (cninfo filings).

name: Larry Connor
current_role: Founder and managing partner, The Connor Group (Dayton, Ohio luxury-apartment investor)
profile: Larry Connor founded The Connor Group in 1991 and bought out his partners in 2003; it owns and operates a ~$5bn portfolio of luxury apartment communities in 12 states, with a reported 30% annual return. An adventurer-philanthropist, he flew on Axiom's Ax-1 mission to the ISS (2022), dove the Mariana Trench (2021) and opened the Greater Dayton School for under-resourced kids in 2024.
interesting_fact: Within days of the 2023 OceanGate Titan implosion he phoned Triton Submarines' Patrick Lahey and funded a $20m two-person sub, the Triton 4000/2 Abyssal Explorer, to show the Titanic wreck can be visited safely and repeatedly.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2023 he set the world record for the highest HALO formation skydive, at 38,139 feet, with four U.S. Air Force pararescue specialists; his first jobs included painting houses and selling 'damaged label' wine to college students.
notes: Very media-friendly and publicity-oriented around his expeditions; strong podcast candidate. Connor Group's published media-inquiries contact is criva@connorgroup.com (company accounts, not personal). Titanic dive status (targeted ~2026) not confirmed.

name: Taylor Swift
current_role: Singer-songwriter and recording artist; owner of her master recordings and catalog
profile: Taylor Swift became a billionaire in 2023, the first musician to reach the ranks primarily on songs and performances, driven by the record-breaking Eras Tour (2023-24) and her catalog. In May 2025 she re-acquired the masters of her first six albums, and released her 12th album, The Life of a Showgirl, in October 2025. She has won 14 Grammys and was Time's 2023 Person of the Year.
interesting_fact: After Midnights (2022) she became the first artist ever to occupy the entire top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 at once; in 2026 she became the youngest female inductee into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
deep_cut_fact: At 14 she signed a songwriting deal with Sony/ATV Tree Music Publishing in Nashville (2004), the youngest writer in the publisher's history; with 'Our Song' she became the youngest person to single-handedly write and sing a No. 1 country single.
notes: Extremely hard to reach; all media goes through her longtime publicist (Tree Paine) and management (13 Management). Unlikely fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast except as a business-of-music case study (masters ownership, Eras Tour economics).

name: David Hearst
current_role: Hearst family heir (beneficiary of the Hearst family trust that controls Hearst Communications); no executive role found
profile: Most likely David Whitmire Hearst Jr., grandson of William Randolph Hearst and son of David Whitmire Hearst (1915-1986), a Hearst Corporation vice president and director. His wealth derives from the family trust that owns privately held Hearst (magazines, newspapers, TV, Fitch, etc.). He appeared on the Forbes 400 in 2004-07; he was reported living in California and Hawaii in 2012.
interesting_fact: His father David and uncle Randolph A. Hearst were twins among William Randolph Hearst's five sons; the family's fortune remains locked in a trust that controls Hearst, one of the largest private US media companies.
notes: Identity not confirmed (Forbes listing gives no first-name detail beyond 'David Hearst'); extremely private with no public role, interviews or channels. Alive status unknown (alive per a 2012 obituary of his mother; nothing later found). Not recommended for outreach.

name: Brian Kim
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of Kakao; head of Kakao's Future Initiative Center (stepped back from frontline management)
profile: Kim Beom-soo ('Brian Kim', b. 1966) grew up poor, earned engineering degrees at Seoul National University, founded online-game portal Hangame in 1998 (merged into NHN/Naver) and in 2010 launched KakaoTalk, now Korea's dominant messenger. Kakao spans Kakao Pay, Kakao Bank, entertainment and mobility; he signed the Giving Pledge in 2021. Since 2026 he has re-emerged publicly, focused on Kakao's AI push.
interesting_fact: He grew up in poverty, paid his way through Seoul National University by private tutoring and sometimes skipped meals to save money, then built Kakao into one of Korea's biggest tech groups.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first company, online game portal Hangame, in 1998 with about $184,000 given to him by friends and family; it later merged with Naver to form NHN, where he became co-CEO.
notes: Hurun lists him under 'Kakao Pay Corp'. Acquitted at first instance (Oct 2025) in the SM Entertainment share case; prosecutors' appeal was pending at Seoul High Court as of mid-2026, so outreach timing is sensitive. Made first public appearance post-acquittal Jan 2026 at Kakao's AI campus. Route via Kakao corporate communications.
